question.text:
Place the following alcohols in decreasing order of rate of dehydration with concentrated H2SO4 :

1. CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3

2. (CH3)2C(OH)CH2CH2CH3

3. (CH3)2C(OH)CH(CH3)2

4. CH3CH2CH(OH)CH(CH3)2

​5. CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2OH

solution.text: The alcohols (3) and (2) are both 3<sup>o</sup>, but alcohol (3) gives a more substituted alkene. Alcohol (4) and (1) are both 2<sup>o</sup>, but alcohol (4) can give a more substituted alkene and alcohol (5) is 1<sup>o</sup>. Rate of dehydration of alcohols with concentrated H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> follows the order 3<sup>o</sup> > 2<sup>o</sup> > 1<sup>o</sup>.
